chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali ibn Ma'bad, on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Khalid As-Sayrafi, who said: Abul Hassan Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever believes in transmigration is an unbeliever. Then he (peace be upon him) added: 'May God damn the exaggerators (Ghulat). I wish they were Magi! I wish they were Christians! I wish they were Qadarites! I wish they were Marji'ites! I wish they were Harawites!' The Imam (peace be upon him) then added: 'Do not associate with or be friends with them, and despise them, as God has despised them.'

key_terms.الْغُلَاة: The exaggerators (sect known for exaggerating in the virtues of the Imams)
key_terms.مُرْجِئَةً: Marji'ites (those who postpone judgment of sinners)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on believers in transmigration according to Imam Ar-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.) identifies belief in transmigration (al-tanasukh)—the soul of one person entering another's body—as a core tenet of the Ghulat (exaggerators), declaring such believers to be unbelievers (kafir). He famously remarks that the Ghulat are worse than Magi, Christians, Qadarites, Marji'ites, and Harawites, emphasizing their unique deviation by instructing the community to avoid intimate association and maintain distinct separation from them.
